title: What food hygiene training does EU Regulation 852/2004 require?
description: What Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 Annex II Chapter XII requires for food handler hygiene and HACCP training in EU food businesses, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 on the hygiene of foodstuffs requires EU food business operators to ensure that food handlers are supervised and instructed or trained in food hygiene commensurate with their work, that people who develop and maintain the HACCP-based procedure are adequately trained in HACCP principles, and that national training rules are met. The duty sits in Annex II, Chapter XII, and sets no fixed hours or refresher interval.
keyTakeaways: Annex II, Chapter XII of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 sets three training duties: hygiene supervision and instruction or training for food handlers, HACCP training for those responsible for the HACCP-based procedure, and compliance with national training rules.
Training must be "commensurate with their work activity": a waiter and a cook need different levels, according to the European Commission's 2022 guidance notice.
Since March 2021, Chapter XIa (food safety culture) also requires management commitment that includes "ensuring that the appropriate training and supervision are in place for personnel".

The Regulation sets no minimum hours, certificate, or refresher interval; the Commission says refresher training and its frequency should be considered according to the needs of the establishment and demonstrated skills.
Formal courses are not mandatory: the Commission says skills can also come from on-the-job training, guides to good practice, and advice from professional bodies or competent authorities.
regulator: Competent authorities designated by each Member State, which carry out official controls under Regulation (EU) 2017/625; the European Commission (Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety) issues guidance
appliesTo: Food business operators at all stages of production, processing, and distribution of food after primary production, including manufacturers, caterers, restaurants, retailers, and distributors
Primary producers, through Annex I, which requires staff handling foodstuffs to be in good health and to undergo training on health risks
Food handlers, their supervisors, and people responsible for developing and maintaining HACCP-based procedures
Not private domestic food preparation or the direct supply of small quantities of primary products, which are excluded by Article 1(2)

sections.heading: What is Regulation 852/2004 and who does it apply to?

blocks.text: [Regulation (EC) No 852/2004](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32004R0852) of April 29, 2004 lays down the general hygiene rules for food business operators across the EU. It has applied since January 1, 2006 and, as a regulation, is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in every Member State without transposition. Article 1(1)(a) sets its starting principle: "primary responsibility for food safety rests with the food business operator."

The Regulation applies to all stages of production, processing, and distribution of food and to exports. Article 4(2) requires operators after primary production to comply with the general hygiene requirements in Annex II, which is where the training chapter sits. Article 5 requires those operators to put in place, implement, and maintain a permanent procedure based on hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) principles.

This page states the position as at November 2026, based on the EUR-Lex [consolidated version of March 24, 2021](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0852-20210324), which EUR-Lex lists as the current consolidated version. That version includes the changes made by [Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/382](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32021R0382), which added food safety culture requirements. Chapter XII itself is unchanged since 2004.

sections.heading: What does Annex II, Chapter XII require?

blocks.text: Chapter XII is short and contains three obligations on the food business operator. The full text reads:

blocks.title: Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Annex II, Chapter XII: Training
blocks.text: "Food business operators are to ensure: 1. that food handlers are supervised and instructed and/or trained in food hygiene matters commensurate with their work activity; 2. that those responsible for the development and maintenance of the procedure referred to in Article 5(1) of this Regulation or for the operation of relevant guides have received adequate training in the application of the HACCP principles; and 3. compliance with any requirements of national law concerning training programmes for persons working in certain food sectors."

blocks.caption: The three training duties in Chapter XII (as at November 2026)
head: Point
Who it covers
What is required
rows: Food handlers
Supervision, and instruction and/or training, in food hygiene matters commensurate with their work activity
People who develop and maintain the HACCP-based procedure under Article 5(1), or who operate relevant guides
Adequate training in the application of the HACCP principles
People working in certain food sectors
Whatever training programs national law requires in that Member State

blocks.text: Two features matter for program design. First, "and/or" means supervision plus instruction can satisfy point 1 for some roles; not every handler needs a course. Second, "commensurate with their work activity" makes the content role based, which is easiest to manage with a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix).

sections.heading: How does the 2021 food safety culture requirement affect training?

blocks.text: Regulation (EU) 2021/382 added Chapter XIa to Annex II, which makes training and supervision part of management's food safety culture commitment. Operators must "establish, maintain and provide evidence of an appropriate food safety culture", including "awareness of food safety hazards and of the importance of food safety and hygiene by all employees in the business".

Under Chapter XIa point 2(d), management commitment includes "ensuring that the appropriate training and supervision are in place for personnel". Point 3 says implementation "shall take account of the nature and size of the food business". The Commission's 2022 notice observes that training "will often be the most important tool to achieve a good food safety culture" and can serve as corrective action when culture assessments find shortcomings.

sections.heading: What does European Commission guidance add?

blocks.text: The [Commission Notice 2022/C 355/01](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52022XC0916(01)) on food safety management systems explains how Chapter XII should be applied. It is guidance, not law, but competent authorities use it.

items: **General versus HACCP training:** "A distinction should be made between training on hygiene in general (all employees) and specific HACCP training." Employees who monitor, manage, or verify critical control points should be trained in HACCP-based procedures appropriate to their tasks.
**Role levels:** "a waiter/waitress will need a certain level of hygiene training, while a cook will need additional training related to the hygienic preparation of food."

**Demonstrated skills:** management "shall make sure that staff taking part in the relevant processes demonstrate sufficient skills" and are aware of hazards, critical points, corrective and preventive measures, and monitoring and recording procedures.

**Broad meaning of training:** appropriate training "does not necessarily involve participation in formal training courses"; skills can come from technical information, advice from professional organizations or competent authorities, on-the-job or in-house training, and guides to good practice.

**Proportionality:** good hygiene practice, prerequisite program, and HACCP training "should be proportionate to the size and the nature of the business" and reflect the specific risks of the activity.

blocks.text: The notice also lists checking "the adequate, training and knowledge on GHP of the personnel or staff" among verification activities, so operators should expect inspectors to test knowledge, not only view certificates.

sections.heading: How often must food hygiene training be refreshed?

blocks.text: Regulation 852/2004 sets no refresher interval and no minimum hours. The Commission's notice says "Possible refresher training and its frequency should be considered according to the needs of the establishment and demonstrated skills."

That makes frequency a documented, risk-based decision. Reasonable triggers include a new starter or role change, a change to the product, process, or HACCP plan (Article 5(2) already requires the procedure to be reviewed when any modification is made), a monitoring failure or complaint traced to handling, and findings from a food safety culture assessment. National rules under Chapter XII point 3 may set fixed requirements for specific sectors, so check the Member State. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: Who enforces the training duty, including in Portugal?

blocks.text: National competent authorities enforce Regulation 852/2004 through official controls, and penalties are set nationally. Article 5(4) requires operators to provide the competent authority with evidence of HACCP compliance in the manner it requires, taking account of the nature and size of the business. Official controls are governed by [Regulation (EU) 2017/625](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32017R0625), whose Article 139 requires Member States to lay down penalties that are "effective, proportionate and dissuasive" for infringements of that Regulation.

In Portugal, the [Autoridade de Segurança Alimentar e Económica (ASAE)](https://www.asae.gov.pt/) is the food and economic safety authority whose inspection plan includes a food area. Portuguese operators should check Portuguese law for any sector-specific training programs that apply under Chapter XII point 3. For the Australian equivalent, see [Food Safety Standard 3.2.2A training](/regulations/food-safety-standard-3-2-2a-training).

sections.heading: How can a food business map Chapter XII to evidence?

blocks.text: Map each duty to an outcome staff can demonstrate and the record an inspector would accept. The table is illustrative, not a Commission template; scale it to the business.

blocks.text: Records should be "commensurate with the nature and size of the food business", the phrase Article 5(2)(g) uses for HACCP documents. For record design, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models hygiene rules, HACCP critical control points, and roles as linked concepts, each with assessment points that show a person can apply the control, not only that they attended. When a HACCP plan changes, the affected roles and assessments are identified from those links. See [operational procedures programs](/programs/operational-procedures).

faqs.q: Does EU law require a food hygiene certificate for every food handler?
faqs.a: No. Chapter XII requires food handlers to be supervised and instructed and/or trained commensurate with their work, and the Commission says appropriate training does not necessarily mean formal courses. Some Member States add national training requirements for certain sectors under Chapter XII point 3, so certificates may be required nationally.

faqs.q: How many hours of food hygiene training does Regulation 852/2004 require?
faqs.a: None are specified. The Regulation sets no hours and no fixed refresher interval. Training must match the work activity, and the Commission's 2022 notice says refresher training and its frequency should be considered according to the establishment's needs and the skills staff demonstrate.

faqs.q: Who needs HACCP training under Regulation 852/2004?
faqs.a: Those responsible for developing and maintaining the HACCP-based procedure under Article 5(1), or for operating relevant guides, must have adequate training in the application of HACCP principles. The Commission adds that employees who monitor, manage, or verify critical control points should be trained in the procedures relevant to their tasks.

faqs.q: Does the food safety culture requirement add new training duties?
faqs.a: It reinforces them. Chapter XIa, added in 2021, requires management commitment that includes ensuring appropriate training and supervision are in place, plus hygiene awareness among all employees. Operators must be able to provide evidence of their food safety culture, which in practice includes training records and assessment results.
